chapter: San Francisco and the postwar slump
title: Postwar collapse of Los Angeles
summary: His father's letter warned him to leave California; back in LA the clubs had closed, and he met Al Hibbler and Al Killian.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: This was February of '46. I'll never forget, my father wrote me a letter. He said, "Look, the war is winding down. Get out of California." He said, "Because it's no good for musicians and entertainers." He had been out here with shows years ago, you know, and he said "It's not the place to be." And sure enough, when we got back to San Francisco, the war was over, and the bottom had dropped out of Los Angeles! All the clubs had closed, you know, and it had just come to a standstill almost.

This is where I first met Al Hibbler. He was living at the Silver Thong(?). And the great Al Killian, the trumpet player, had been doing some work for Norman Granz on the Jazz At The Philharmonic, and decided to stay out here.
